name: a_ai_capex
prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Friday October 16, 2026. Topic: AI capex & cloud.

Window: Thursday October 15, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Friday October 16, 2026 02:03 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. Anything published after 02:03 ET on Friday October 16, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
Hyperscaler capex estimates and commentary (with firm/analyst name), AI cloud and compute deals ($ value, term), data-center projects, delays or cancellations, AI financing (bonds, converts, private credit), OpenAI/Anthropic/xAI funding and compute commitments, GPU cloud pricing.

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.

## **AMZN** / **MSFT** / **GOOGL** / **META** / ORCL — AI Infrastructure
- Big Four 2026 capital-expenditure guidance was reported at approximately **$725 billion** combined for Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet and Meta; adding Oracle’s reported **$50 billion** forecast brought the top-five estimate to approximately **$775 billion** (Au79 Macro Research, Oct. 15; publish time not stated).[8]
- Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said Trainium could save Amazon **tens of billions of dollars in annual capex** at scale and provide a **several-hundred-basis-point operating-margin advantage** versus relying on other chips for inference (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15 08:34 ET).[4]

## **IREN** — AI Infrastructure
- IREN’s announced AI-cloud contracts exceeded **$13 billion**, including a **$9.7 billion, five-year Microsoft contract** covering **200 MW** across four installments; the first installment was delivered in **August 2026** (MarketBeat, Oct. 14; updated Oct. 16, publish time not stated).[10]
- IREN was targeting approximately **300 MW of AI IT capacity by year-end 2026** and **800 MW by the end of 2027**, with **5 GW of power secured** across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific (MarketBeat, Oct. 14; updated Oct. 16, publish time not stated).[10]
- IREN’s reported NVIDIA-related expansion included up to **5 GW of NVIDIA-based capacity**, centered on the **2 GW Sweetwater, Texas** facility, plus a **$3.4 billion** contract to provide AI-cloud capacity for NVIDIA’s internal workloads (MarketBeat, Oct. 14; updated Oct. 16, publish time not stated).[10]
- A report linked IREN’s previously announced multiyear frontier-AI-lab contract to Anthropic, but the customer identity was described as unconfirmed [rumor] (MarketBeat, Oct. 14; updated Oct. 16, publish time not stated).[10]

## Anthropic — AI Compute
- Anthropic reportedly told investors that third-quarter revenue reached **$16.8 billion**, up from **$11.6 billion in Q2 2026** and **$4.7 billion in Q1 2026**, and that it was profitable on an adjusted basis [report] (Resultsense, Oct. 15; publish time not stated).[6]
- Anthropic reportedly raised **$65 billion** in a Series H financing at a **$965 billion post-money valuation** [report] (Resultsense, Oct. 15; publish time not stated).[6]
- Anthropic reportedly had at least **$518 billion** of cloud, compute and infrastructure commitments over **10 years**, including commitments involving Google and Amazon [report] (Resultsense, Oct. 15; publish time not stated).[6]
- Anthropic reportedly secured all of SpaceX’s Colossus 1 capacity, described as more than **220,000 GPUs**, and doubled Claude Code rate limits for Pro, Max and Enterprise customers [report] (Resultsense, Oct. 15; publish time not stated).[6]
- Anthropic reportedly signed a **$45 billion, six-year** deal with Nscale [report] (Marcus Today, Oct. 15; publish time not stated).[2]

## OpenAI — AI Compute / Internet & Platforms
- OpenAI, Anthropic and the Simons Foundation announced a combined **$15 million** commitment for mathematics research responding to AI-generated mathematical results; OpenAI’s contribution was reported at **$5 million**, alongside model access and computing resources (WebProNews, Oct. 16; publish time not stated).[5]
- OpenAI’s reported compute commitments included approximately **$300 billion with Oracle**, **$250 billion with Azure**, **$138 billion with AWS** and **$22 billion with CoreWeave** [report] (Marcus Today, Oct. 15; publish time not stated).[2]
- OpenAI’s reported hardware commitments included **10 GW from NVIDIA**, **6 GW from AMD** and **10 GW of custom chips from Broadcom** [report] (Marcus Today, Oct. 15; publish time not stated).[2]

## **MSFT** / **AMZN** / **GOOGL** — AI Infrastructure
- Microsoft was reported to own approximately **27% of OpenAI** and to have up to **$5 billion invested in Anthropic** [report] (Marcus Today, Oct. 15; publish time not stated).[2]
- Amazon and Alphabet were reported to jointly hold approximately **30% of Anthropic**, while AWS hosted more than **$100 billion** of Anthropic work and approximately **$138 billion** of OpenAI work [report] (Marcus Today, Oct. 15; publish time not stated).[2]
- Microsoft was reported to rent AI capacity from Nebius under a **$17.4 billion** commitment and from IREN under a **$9.7 billion** commitment [report] (Marcus Today, Oct. 15; publish time not stated).[2]

## **NVDA** — AI Compute
- NVIDIA pledged **$250 million over five years**, or **$50 million annually**, for UK agentic-AI safety and security research through UK-based NVIDIA Cloud Partners (Another Daily AI Newsletter, Oct. 15; publish time not stated).[1]
- NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang said NVIDIA revenue per gigawatt had increased from approximately **$18 billion to more than $40 billion** as the company added networking, CPUs, storage and security; the commentary was published Oct. 15 and updated Oct. 16, before the cutoff (PJFP, Oct. 15; updated Oct. 16, publish time not stated).[9]

## **COREWEAVE** — AI Financing / AI Infrastructure
- CoreWeave was reported to have **$35.6 billion of debt**, Q2 adjusted operating income of **$128 million**, Q2 net interest expense of **$640 million**, and first-half free cash flow of approximately **negative $10.5 billion** [report] (Marcus Today, Oct. 15; publish time not stated).[3]
- CoreWeave’s 2026 capex guidance was reported at **$35 billion–$39 billion** [report] (Marcus Today, Oct. 15; publish time not stated).[3]
- NVIDIA was reported to own approximately **10.7% of CoreWeave Class A shares** and to have provided a **$6.3 billion capacity backstop** [report] (Marcus Today, Oct. 15; publish time not stated).[2]

## AI Financing — AI Infrastructure
- Morgan Stanley was reported to estimate approximately **$570 billion of global AI-related debt in 2026**, including bonds, loans and private credit [report] (Marcus Today, Oct. 15; publish time not stated).[3]

## **AVGO** / **INTC** — AI Infrastructure
- Broadcom CEO Hock Tan and Intel executives were cited in an Oct. 15 report discussing **capital availability** as a constraint on AI data-center expansion; the report did not provide a new company-specific capex figure (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15 08:34 ET).[4]
